question.worked_solution:
To determine whether the sequence converges or diverges, we need to determine the limit of the sequence as $n$ approaches infinity:

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12n+1}{3n}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is $3n,$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by $n$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{a}_{n} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12n+1}{3n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12n}{n}+\frac{1}{n})}{\frac{3n}{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{12+\frac{1}{n}}{3} \\  & =\frac{12+0}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges, and its limit is $4.$
